plot: You land in New York at 7 AM but your body clock says 4 AM. Cortez's master clock only resets from the light report, Melly (melatonin) keeps announcing nighttime, the clock moves about an hour a day, flying east is harder because the clock runs a bit longer than 24 hours, Gus wants lunch at midnight, Liv's organ clock lags behind. Three days later the clock matches the sun. Tease: a knuckle crack.

script.title: Jet Lag Inside You: LA to New York in 5 Hours

episode.action: land in New York from Los Angeles on a red-eye

beats.title: Jet Lag Inside You: LA to New York in 5 Hours

beats.say: It's seven in the morning in New York. My clock says four. Somebody explain why we're awake!
The sun moved! The sun just moved three hours and nobody told us!
Right. Five hours in a plane, three time zones, and my master clock hasn't read the news.
beats.label: Master clock: a tiny group in the brain

beats.say: Also, my night shift runs on low output. Nobody told the traveler. I'm closed.
beats.label: Kidneys: make less urine at night

beats.say: Hello, hello. Melly here. Melatonin. I get released when it's dark, and I tell everybody it's nighttime.
beats.label: Melatonin: the brain's night signal

beats.say: Right now, my gland thinks it's four in the morning. So I'm doing my job. Sleepy time, everyone! Loudly!
Melly! It's morning! There are bagels outside! Please wake up!
Melly! Quiet! There's a morning meeting and the sun's already out!
I have one job, boss. Dark means go time. Nobody gave me an update.
Eyes, send the light report. The retina is the only one who tells my master clock what time it really is.
beats.label: Retina: light sensor wired to the clock

beats.say: Memo from the eyes: bright morning sun, priority one, in all capital letters!
Excellent. Clock, reset to seven AM.
The clock moved to... four oh five.
Five minutes?! That's it?! It only moves about an hour a day! We're three hours behind!
I ran the numbers. Three time zones, about three days. I made a spreadsheet.
Why is flying east so rough? Because our clock runs a little longer than twenty-four hours. Stretching a day is easy. Shrinking it is not.
beats.label: Flying east: usually harder than west

beats.say: So going west is like sleeping in, and going east is like waking up early on purpose?
Exactly. And my body is a middle manager who hates both.
Lunch break! Wait, why's the kitchen closed? My clock says it's the middle of the night.
beats.label: Gut rhythms: also follow a body clock

beats.say: Travel breakfast at seven? My acid isn't even dressed! I'm still in my slippers!
Then by midnight, I'm starving. It's a snack crisis.
Cortez shifts his clock. I have my own clock. It doesn't take orders by memo.
beats.label: Organ clocks: each one keeps its own rhythm

beats.say: I'll catch up. Eventually. Organs adjust at different speeds. That's why you feel off all over.
My heart rate dips at night and climbs by day. I'm running a day shift on a night schedule!
Sleepy at noon? DENIED. Nap request? DENIED. Everything's denied.
Bad news, boss. It's noon in New York, but my records say nine. Bedtime announcements are still going out.
Day two. The clock moved one more hour. I'm learning patience. I hate it.
Hello! We have no clock! We breathe when asked! Ask us again!
Day three. My budget's up on both sides, and I still have no idea what time it is.
Clock check. Light report says morning. And the master clock says... seven AM!
It matches the sun! Somebody get me a bagel!
Almost. I'm still half an hour behind. Don't wait up.
My part's done. Dark means night, light means morning. I'll announce at the right time from here on.
Everyone, back to normal. Except Gus. He's hungry.
Next time: a knuckle crack. I heard a pop, and it wasn't me.

fact.title: REAL BODY NOTE
lines: Morning light is your clock's reset signal.
Flying east usually feels harder than west.
fact.source: NIGMS: Circadian Rhythms; StatPearls: Jet Lag

long.title: Jet Lag Inside You: LA to New York in 5 Hours
long.description:
You land in New York at 7 AM, but your body clock says 4 AM. Cortez's master clock hasn't read the news, Melly the night-signal drop keeps announcing bedtime, Liv's liver clock refuses to take memos, and Gus wants lunch at midnight.
A funny, body-accurate look at jet lag: the master clock, melatonin, morning light, and why flying east is harder than flying west.

Real body notes (sources): NIGMS, Circadian Rhythms fact sheet: https://www.nigms.nih.gov/education/fact-sheets/Pages/circadian-rhythms.aspx ; NCBI Bookshelf, StatPearls: Jet Lag Disorder (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books) ; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e, Endocrine System (openstax.org).
Entertainment and general education, not medical advice. Original characters, animated in Blender.
